# How to Map Any Legacy Code Base in Seconds! (Understand Anything)

The video features Understand Anything, an open source plugin that combines language models and static analysis to mount an interactive map of a code base. Displays the agent pipeline, guided tours, change impact analysis and cost in first scan tokens.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on August 26, 2026 (7 min 1 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_dku8xoMWY

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The house in the dark

Getting into a big, unknown software project is like walking into a house in the dark. The video features a tool that promises to map the entire code [00:00].

The classic problem: clone a legacy repository of 200,000 lines without the original engineers, and try to add a feature. It becomes an archaeological excavation, and it is not known where to begin [00:22].

The proposal is to have an interactive map that teaches the code base from the first minute, instead of using AI agents that guess solutions without architecture context [00:42].

## What Understand Anything is

Understand Anything is an open source viewer [00:42]. It's a plugin for Claude Code that combines language models with traditional static analysis and builds a live and interactive map of the entire project [01:03].

According to the video, the tool went from 14,000 stars in GitHub in a few weeks [01:25]. On the project page, read on 11/19/2026, the number is already over 90 thousand.

Although born as Claude Code plugin, it also works with Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Codex and OpenCode [01:45].

## From code to meaning

Traditional code graphs show only the structure: where the files and functions are, and who cares who. It is a map without legend [02:08].

Understand Anything focuses on meaning: business logic, authentication flows and user life cycle [02:28].

Behind, an AI agent pipeline works as an assembly line [02:28]:

1. A scanner discovers the files and frameworks [02:48].
2. An analyzer extracts the functions [02:48].
3. A third agent identifies the layers of architecture [02:48].
4. A builder generates guided learning tours [02:48].
5. A reviewer validates everything, to ensure that references make sense [02:48].

In a medium project, such as the demonstration of Google microservices, the tool groups hundreds of files into layers separated by colors: 34 front-end, 108 back-end logic, 105 Kubernetes configuration and 33 CI/CD infrastructure [03:09].

## Three use cases

With the map, you can attack three major wastes of time [03:30]:

- Guided tours generated on time, in place of outdated documentation [03:30].
- Full context for AI agents [03:30].
- Refactoring more safely [03:30].

Impact analysis shows, before confirming the change, which parts of the system a change will affect. Avoids the nightmare of changing a harmless line and breaking the entire system [03:51].

The interface adjusts the level of detail to whom it uses. A product manager can ask a common language question about a business flow and receive a response based on the real code [04:13].

## The cost in tokens

Not everything is perfect. Constructing a graph of knowledge of this size consumes much processing and many tokens [04:35].

According to the video, an average project can take up to 30 minutes and consume 25% of the requirement limit of a premium AI plan in a single execution [04:57].

The relief is that the result is saved in a file on the computer itself, and the high cost only comes in the first scan [04:57]. Then the updates are incremental: only the changed files are reviewed, with parallel analysis [05:18].

The tool has MIT license, free and free [05:39].

## The Future of Code Reading

The workflow leaves the reading of directory structures and goes to the understanding of the system behavior [05:39].

According to the video, the graph gathers more than 26 file types: infrastructure such as Docker and Terraform, SQL queries and Markdown documentation [05:59].

The productivity lesson: Getting quick context replaces jumping blindly between files. Before touching anything, see the overview [06:21].

The final question: If AI maps the meaning of the repositories, will it be necessary to read legacy code again in the crude way of the past? [06:43]

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Understand Anything only work on Claude Code?

Nope. He was born as a Claude Code plugin, but also works with Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Codex and OpenCode [01:45].

### Why is the first analysis expensive?

Because building the whole project graph consumes many tokens. Then only the changed files are reviewed [04:57].

## About the video

You've just joined a new development team, clone the repository and come across a complex system of 200,000 lines of code.
Where do you start? Instead of reading blind code and getting lost in outdated documentation, Understand Anything offers a true interactive map that teaches how your system architecture works.

This open source plugin combines LLM intelligence and static analysis to build a live, visual and fully navigable map of your project, providing clear explanations for each component. It works integrated with tools such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI.

Main features demonstrated in this video:
Interactive Knowledge Graph: view the structure and dependencies automatically organized by architectural layers (such as API, Service, Data and UI).
Explanations Simplified: Each file, class or function receives a description in natural language so that anyone (junior developers or Product Managers) understands their function in the system.
Guided Learning Tours (/understand-onboard): step-by-step routes generated by AI that teach the operation of the system in logical order of dependency, reducing the time from week to minute onboarding.
Change Impact Analysis (/understand-diff): See in advance which parts and flows of the system will be affected by your changes before committing to the code base.
Preparation for AI Agents: Deliver a structured system map to your coding AI tools, preventing them from just guessing the changes.

Official References and Links:
Source code in GitHub: https://github.com/Lum1104/Understand-Anything (or official repository of the organization: https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything)
Official website and demo: https://understand-anything.com
Community Analysis Video (Better Stack): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VmIUXVlt7_I

If you know other developers or teams who suffer to decipher complex or legacy code bases, share this video with them!
